          Chelsea 5-1 Bournemouth Stats: Jordan Henderson Rolls Back the Years to Inspire Rout
        
      
                          
                      Oct 10, 2026
          
                      Chloe Horswill / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Veteran midfielder Jordan Henderson scored twice and set up another as Chelsea ran riot against a beleaguered Bournemouth.
Jordan Henderson scored twice and teed up another as he set Chelsea on their way to a thumping 5-1 win over Bournemouth in the Premier League.
Chelsea needed fewer than three minutes to race into a 2-0 lead, with Henderson and Morgan Rogers both scoring early, while João Pedro added their third within the first minute of the second half.
Evanilson pulled one back for Bournemouth, but João Pedro and Henderson both scored again to get Chelsea their first top-flight win since the end of August.

Chelsea flew out of the blocks, and Henderson took just 66 seconds to break the deadlock. Cole Palmer – for whom a new eight-year deal was announced on Saturday – powered forward before laying the ball off for Henderson for a first-time finish that flew in off the post.

And just 83 seconds after the restart, Chelsea had a second. Pedro Neto was denied by Djordje Petrovic, but the Blues kept it alive, with Henderson helping it to Rogers, who floated a shot into the goal via a flick off António Silva head to help it over the goalkeeper.
The fast start continued as Bournemouth exploited space down the left, but Rayan was selfish and watched his effort sail into the stands.

Only twice before in Premier League history has a team gone 2-0 up earlier than Chelsea vs Bournemouth today (2:29).▪️ Leicester vs Derby County, April 1998▪️ Luton vs Brighton, Jan 2024Both of those sides went on to win 4-0. pic.twitter.com/92sFSHChbh

Emiliano Martínez ensured Chelsea went into the break with their two-goal cushion, making a double save to keep out Rayan and Ryan Christie just after the half-hour mark before holding onto Silva's header.
And Chelsea wasted no time in the second half, either. Within 30 seconds, João Pedro had the ball in the back of the net after Neto latched onto a poor attempted clearance from Silva.

But Bournemouth responded well as they exploited Chelsea's set-piece struggles. Moisés Caicedo tried to hook a corner clear, but Evanilson stuck out a leg to send it flying past Martínez 51 minutes in.

It took João Pedro just 16 minutes to restore Chelsea's three-goal advantage, with Pep Chavarria taking Bournemouth's defence out of the game with his low cross, and the Brazilian was on hand to emphatically turn it in.
And Henderson added the late gloss. Palmer won the free-kick, but caught Bournemouth out by not taking it, and Henderson curled it over the wall and past Petrovic at his near post.

After failing to win three straight Premier League games before the international break, Chelsea returned to action with a bang and even more early goals. There have been five goals scored in the opening three minutes of games in the competition this term, and Chelsea have scored four of them.

Henderson got his first goal for the Blues in the process, becoming the club's oldest English goalscorer in the Premier League (36 years, 115 days) since John Terry against Watford in May 2017 (36y 159d).

His assist for Rogers meant that only once (Emile Heskey against Derby County in April 1998 – in the opening two minutes) has a player both scored and assisted in a Premier League game earlier than Henderson (2:29).

36 – Jordan Henderson (36y 115d) is the oldest @ChelseaFC player to be directly involved in 3+ goals in a Premier League match (2 goals, 1 assist), and oldest for any side since Cristiano Ronaldo in April 2022 (37 v Norwich).Twilight. pic.twitter.com/OdCRuSQRTi

And he also became the oldest Chelsea player to be directly involved in three goals in a Premier League game, overtaking Gianluca Vialli (33y 245d), and the oldest for any side since Cristiano Ronaldo in April 2022 (37 v Norwich City).

This was only the second time Henderson has registered three goal involvements in a single game in the competition, last doing so back in April 2013 for Liverpool against Newcastle United (also two goals, one assist).

João Pedro missed out for Brazil during the international break through injury but looked strong on his return to the side; only Bruno Fernandes (22) has now been involved in more top-flight goals in 2026 than the Brazilian (19 – 14 goals, five assists).
